sources.title: 7 Principles for Coaches: Vision & Scanning
sources.verificationMethod: Fetched directly (curl, browser User-Agent) and read the full extracted page text before citing.
sources.exactQuote: When scanning or looking around on the ice, players should focus on two main sources of information: where their teammates are and where the opposition's pressure is coming from. Being able to quickly identify these factors will assist in making better decisions with the puck under pressure.
sources.honestLimitation: This source supports 'identify teammate position + opposition pressure to inform the decision' as a real, named coaching principle. It does NOT itself use hypothetical/'Suppose the defender moves' framing -- the cause-and-effect family's specific instructional device (state one explicit hypothetical change, ask the learner to update their read) is this project's own original design layered on top of the source's general scanning principle, not something quoted or implied verbatim by Hockey Canada. Flagging this distinction rather than overclaiming direct textual support.

sources.title: Timbits U7 Hockey: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.section: Cross-ice dimensions Q&A; crease/face-off-circle placement Q&A; program-priority framing paragraph
sources.verificationMethod: Fetched directly (curl, browser User-Agent) and read the full extracted page text before citing.
sources.exactQuote: The average dimensions of a regular ice surface in Canada are 200 feet by 85 feet... The cross-ice surface can be a maximum of 100 feet by 60 feet if the dividers are placed at the blue-line. ... Each net should be placed just inside the face-off circle, which will provide a small marking to aid the goaltender in positioning themselves.
sources.honestLimitation: The same FAQ also states: "the primary focus on age-appropriate training and programming needs to be on skill development in skating, puck control, passing, receiving and shooting. Concepts like offside, icing, positional play and face-offs can be introduced at a later age." This is a real tension worth surfacing, not resolving unilaterally: the source confirms the blue line and face-off circle are real, physically present U7 landmarks (supporting pure landmark-naming), but also explicitly deprioritizes teaching 'positional play' and 'face-off' CONCEPTS (i.e., the rules/procedures) at this age in favour of raw skill reps. This draft pair is scoped to bare landmark identification only (naming a line/circle), not face-off procedure or positional-play tactics, which is a narrower claim than what the caution addresses -- but a qualified reviewer should confirm that distinction holds before real authoring, since it is this session's own reading, not something the source states explicitly.
